questions.question: After finishing a pre-trip inspection, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the rear shut-off valves open.
Leave the emergency line valve open.

questions.explanation: Open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves to check that air reaches all brakes on all trailers. You will hear air escaping. Close both shut-off valves before you start driving.

questions.question: Who must identify the hazard class of materials being shipped?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for identifying the product ID number, shipping name, hazard class, packing group, and correct packaging, labels, marking, and placards.

questions.question: Your wheel bearing and seals should be:
questions.explanation: During an inspection, check that the wheel bearing and seals are not leaking.

questions.question: What does rust around wheel nuts indicate?
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check how tight the nuts are if you see rust in that area.

questions.question: What is a Class 7 hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Radioactive materials are Class 7 hazardous materials.

questions.question: What should you do if you are unsure how to put out a vehicle fire?
questions.explanation: If you are not sure which fire extinguisher to use on a vehicle fire, especially a hazardous materials fire, leave the area and wait for firefighters to arrive.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out of the vehicle and call for assistance.
Continue trying to get your vehicle off the tracks until you are successful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for assistance.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks, leave immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on the signposts or signal box at the crossing. Call 911 or another emergency number.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving is:

options.text: Discouraged, as there is little you can do about something far up the road.
Encouraged to help you spot hazards early.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encouraged to help you spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead of their vehicle. This gives drivers time to spot hazards early and respond safely.

questions.question: How should you apply the brakes using the stab braking method?

options.text: With about half of your usual force.
As hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Fully until the wheels lock up. Release until the wheels roll again, then repeat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fully until the wheels lock up. Release until the wheels roll again, then repeat.
questions.explanation: The stab braking method means fully applying the brakes until they lock. Then release them until the wheels start rolling again. Repeat this process.

questions.question: When starting a truck with a trailer, how do you know if the ABS is not working?

options.text: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the right side of the trailer flashes three times.
All the rear lights flash and then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, the dash lights should come on and then turn off. If the ABS malfunction light stays on, the system is not working. For a truck with a trailer, if the yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on after starting, the ABS is not working.

questions.question: When backing, you should:

options.text: Move quickly to get out of the way of other drivers.
Try not to use your mirrors.

questions.explanation: Backing a large truck is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. If you must back up, use a helper if you can.

questions.question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Plan trips without allocating extra time for traffic.
Drive slowly in the left lane.
Not make gestures to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not make gestures to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To avoid being an aggressive driver, plan trips with realistic time. Allow extra time for traffic. Do not tailgate. Do not drive slowly in the left lane. Do not make hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: When nearing a construction worker who is close to the road, you should:

options.text: Wait until the construction is complete before proceeding.

questions.explanation: When driving through work zones, slow down when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: Starting in which year were newly manufactured trailers required to have ABS?
questions.explanation: All trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 items should not be placed in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Cargo heaters are not always allowed. Do not use heaters when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: In addition to reading the manual, the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials is to:
questions.explanation: The manual has all information needed to pass the hazardous materials test. But you should also read federal and state rules about transporting hazardous materials. Take hazardous materials training courses to learn more.

questions.question: The more alcohol in the body:

options.text: The quicker the liver will digest the alcohol.
The less effect the alcohol will have on the individual.
The longer it will take to remove the alcohol from the body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer it will take to remove the alcohol from the body.
questions.explanation: The body removes alcohol at a fixed rate. More alcohol means it takes longer to remove from your system.

questions.question: Move over laws require:

options.text: Trucks to use the left lane.
All vehicles to vacate the lane closest to an emergency vehicle that is stopped with its lights flashing.
All vehicles to use the left lane.
All vehicles to move to the left lane if a flatbed trailer is in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles to vacate the lane closest to an emergency vehicle that is stopped with its lights flashing.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on the roadside, move out of the lane next to it if you can do so safely. If you cannot move over safely, slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: If a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working:

options.text: The truck will not have any brakes.
The truck should be driven only at slow speeds.
The truck will still have brakes.
The truck will lack brakes on its left side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: If the ABS system fails, the vehicle will still have normal brakes. Drive and brake as you normally would.

questions.question: To help your vehicle be seen by others:

options.text: Headlights should be turned off during the day.
Headlights should be covered with grease.
Headlights should only be used in the rain.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlights clean so they shine brightly. This helps other drivers see your vehicle.
